INTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS MATTER AS MUCH AS EXTERNAL - general alarm, public address, bridge/engine room/steering gear telephones independent of main power. MOST EMERGENCIES ARE LOST INTERNALLY
COMPATIBILITY with rescue coordination centres, assisting ships and helicopters, including on-scene frequencies and language

steps.title: Item (iii) - dealing with the media
points: THIS IS A COMPANY FUNCTION, NOT A SHIPBOARD ONE - say so first
A SINGLE AUTHORISED SPOKESPERSON named in the plan; ALL other personnel refer every enquiry to that person
THE MASTER AND CREW DO NOT SPEAK TO THE PRESS - partial information, fully occupied, and anything said becomes the company's position
A PREPARED HOLDING STATEMENT issued quickly - incident occurred, company responding, safety of those on board is the priority, more to follow. SPEED MATTERS MORE THAN COMPLETENESS
FACTS ONLY - no speculation as to cause, no damage or spill estimates before established, NO ADMISSION OF LIABILITY; legal and P&I advice first
NAMES ARE NEVER RELEASED BEFORE THE NEXT OF KIN HAVE BEEN INFORMED - the rule that links (iii) and (iv)
MEDIA TRAINING for the spokesperson and a single controlled channel of release
MONITOR what is published, including social media; correct significant factual errors; assume crew posts will appear and cover it in crew briefing
COORDINATE with flag, coastal State, salvors, charterers, class and P&I so statements do not conflict; do not prejudice the safety investigation
KEEP THE CREW AND THE OFFICE INFORMED - an organisation that learns of its own casualty from a news bulletin loses confidence in its management

steps.title: Item (iv) - dealing with the next of kin
points: ONE PRINCIPLE GOVERNS: THE FAMILY MUST HEAR IT FROM THE COMPANY FIRST, FROM A PERSON, AND ACCURATELY
ACCURATE CURRENT NEXT-OF-KIN RECORDS - name, relationship, address, telephone, language - reviewed at every crew change and IMMEDIATELY RETRIEVABLE OUT OF HOURS
NAMED, TRAINED PERSONNEL make contact - never the switchboard - and where possible in the family's own language
CONTACT AS SOON AS THE FACTS ARE VERIFIED, and before the names reach the press; verify who you are speaking to before disclosing
SAY ONLY WHAT IS KNOWN - no speculation, no minimising, no assurances that may prove false; say when you will call again AND THEN CALL
A SINGLE NAMED POINT OF CONTACT for each family, with a direct number
PRACTICAL AND WELFARE SUPPORT - travel, accommodation, documents and visas, repatriation, interpreters, counselling - offered rather than waited for
CLEAR PROMPT INFORMATION ON ENTITLEMENTS handled with the P&I club, without pressing anyone to sign while in shock
PROTECT THE FAMILY FROM THE PRESS - no names before they are informed; warn them they may be approached and offer help
KEEP CONTACT UP through the response, the investigation and afterwards; name who is responsible
DO NOT MAKE ADMISSIONS - compassion and liability are separate
CLOSE: (i) and (ii) are how the response is DELIVERED; (iii) and (iv) are how the company is JUDGED; and only 8.2 drills test whether any of it works

questions.understand_first: The examiner has taken his opening sentence straight out of the safety management code, and the sentence is doing more work than it looks. It does not say the ship must be able to cope. It says the shore organisation must be able to respond at any time - meaning that at three in the morning on a public holiday, somebody with authority must pick up the telephone. That is the whole idea, and once you see it the four items the question lists stop being a random collection. Two of them are about getting help to the ship: a reliable way for the Master to reach a decision-maker, and equipment that still works when the power has gone and the fire is in the space where the radio used to be. The other two are about people who are nowhere near the ship. The press will publish something within the hour whether or not the company says anything, and if several people give slightly different accounts the company loses control of the story permanently. And the families will find out somehow - and if they find it out from a news bulletin, or from another seafarer's wife, no amount of competent fire-fighting will repair that. So the thread is this: an emergency is not only a technical event to be managed but a set of relationships to be held together, and every one of those relationships runs down a communication channel that either was set up in advance or was not. Nothing here can be improvised, which is why the code also insists the whole thing be rehearsed.
questions.memory_cue: The Code first: IDENTIFY, DRILL, RESPOND ANY TIME (1), propped up by DP, MASTER, LANGUAGE, REVIEW (3). Then note the four items are two pairs - INWARD (4, 5) is how the response is delivered, OUTWARD (6, 7) is how the company is judged. Office is WHO, HOW, WHAT, HOW OFTEN (4). Equipment is WORKS, POWERED, PORTABLE, TESTED, MANNED, INTERNAL (5). Press is ONE VOICE, FAST, FACTS ONLY (6). Families are FROM US, FROM A PERSON, FIRST, AND TRUE (7). The hinge between the last two: no names before the families know (6).

quick_revision.recall_15s: THE STEM IS ISM 8.3. Section 8: 8.1 identify potential emergency shipboard situations and establish procedures to respond; 8.2 establish programmes for drills and exercises; 8.3 the SMS provides measures ensuring the Company's ORGANIZATION can respond AT ANY TIME to hazards, accidents and emergencies involving its ships. Two words carry it: the Company's organization (shore, not ship) and at any time (round the clock). SUPPORTING SECTIONS: 3 responsibility, authority and interrelation defined and documented, adequate shore-based support; 4 Designated Person - link between Company and ship, direct access to the highest level of management; 5 Master's overriding authority and right to request the Company's assistance; 6 able to communicate effectively, SMS information in a working language understood; 9 and 12 non-conformity reporting and Company review. IMPORTANCE: a plan that cannot be activated is not a plan; the ship cannot resolve a serious casualty alone; delay is the cost; information degrades under stress and in a second language; bad external communication is a second, self-inflicted emergency; communication failure is a recurring causal factor. (i) SHIP-OFFICE: written procedure in the SMS · 24-hour number answered by a PERSON · duty roster and call-out list with alternates · DP as primary route, ERT on a defined trigger · standard initial report (ship, position, time, nature, casualties, pollution, damage/stability, weather, action taken, assistance required, caller) · agreed reporting interval so silence is a signal · multiple independent means in stated order · one point of contact each way · timed log both ends · Master's overriding authority respected · maintained shore contact list. (ii) EQUIPMENT: appropriate to trade, working, available at all times · GMDSS functions - alerting, SAR coordinating, on-scene, locating, MSI, general · emergency power, charged batteries, dispersed siting · portables - intrinsically safe for teams, survival craft VHF, EPIRB, SART, allocated in advance · scheduled testing recorded, in the PMS · defect reporting with stated alternatives · enough qualified operators · instructions posted at the station · INTERNAL - general alarm, PA, bridge/ER/steering telephones independent of main power. Most emergencies are lost internally · compatibility with RCC, assisting ships, helicopters. (iii) MEDIA - a COMPANY function: ONE authorised spokesperson, everyone else refers · Master and crew say nothing · prepared holding statement, fast - incident, responding, safety is the priority, more to follow · facts only, no cause, no quantities, NO ADMISSION, legal and P&I advice first · NO NAMES BEFORE NEXT OF KIN ARE INFORMED · media training, single channel · monitor including social media, assume crew posts · coordinate with flag, coastal State, salvors, class, P&I; do not prejudice the safety investigation · keep crew and office informed. (iv) NEXT OF KIN - from us, from a person, first, and true: accurate records retrievable out of hours · named trained callers, family's language · as soon as verified, before the press · say only what is known, say when you will call again and do · one named contact per family · travel, documents, repatriation, interpreters, counselling · clear entitlements via P&I, no signing under shock · shield them from the press · keep contact up · no admissions. The Code requires procedures to EXIST; it does not prescribe their content - say so.

critical_numbers: ISM Code section 8 - three paragraphs: 8.1 identify and establish procedures, 8.2 drills and exercises, 8.3 respond at any time
ISM Code section 4 - Designated Person, direct access to the highest level of management
ISM Code section 5 - the Master's overriding authority

quick_revision.critical_regulation: ISM Code paragraph 8.3 - the safety management system should provide for measures ensuring that the Company's organization can respond at any time to hazards, accidents and emergency situations involving its ships. Read with paragraph 8.1, requiring the Company to identify potential emergency shipboard situations and establish procedures to respond to them, and paragraph 8.2, requiring programmes for drills and exercises. Support comes from section 4, under which the Designated Person is the link between the Company and those on board with direct access to the highest level of management, and section 5, which requires a clear statement of the Master's overriding authority and his right to request the Company's assistance as may be necessary.
quick_revision.major_trap: Answering only half the question. The stem prints two demands - underline the importance of communication in emergency preparedness, and state the measures required for four named items - and a candidate who gives four lists without the argument, or the argument with four thin lists, has answered part of it. The substantive traps are: not recognising that the opening sentence is ISM paragraph 8.3 and writing a general management essay instead; treating media handling as the Master's job when it is a company function with a single authorised spokesperson; releasing names before the next of kin are informed; forgetting internal communications under the equipment limb when most emergencies are lost internally; answering the equipment limb with GMDSS carriage requirements instead of the measures asked for; and presenting media and next-of-kin procedures as ISM requirements when the Code requires only that procedures exist and says nothing about their content.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give the route for the emergency-preparedness communication question.
retrieval_cards.answer: 1 The stem is ISM 8.3, and section 8 in full. 2 Why communication is the load-bearing element. 3 The supporting ISM sections - 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 12. 4 Ship to office. 5 Communication equipment. 6 Media. 7 Next of kin.
retrieval_cards.why: Steps 1 to 3 answer the 'underline the importance' half; steps 4 to 7 carry most of the marks.

retrieval_cards.prompt: State the three paragraphs of ISM Code section 8.
retrieval_cards.answer: 8.1 - the Company should identify potential emergency shipboard situations, and establish procedures to respond to them. 8.2 - the Company should establish programmes for drills and exercises to prepare for emergency actions. 8.3 - the safety management system should provide for measures ensuring that the Company's organization can respond at any time to hazards, accidents and emergency situations involving its ships.
retrieval_cards.why: Three sentences for a sixteen-mark question, and the opening line of the stem is the third of them.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which two words in ISM 8.3 carry the whole question, and why?
retrieval_cards.answer: 'The Company's organization' - the paragraph is about the shore side, not the ship. And 'at any time' - not office hours. Together they mean somebody with authority must be reachable round the clock, which is why the answer's first measure is a 24-hour number answered by a person.
retrieval_cards.why: It converts a quoted sentence into an argument and explains why the question then asks about the office and the families.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which other ISM sections support emergency communication, and what does each contribute?
retrieval_cards.answer: Section 3 - responsibility, authority and interrelation of all personnel defined and documented, with adequate resources and shore-based support. Section 4 - the Designated Person, the link between Company and ship, with direct access to the highest level of management. Section 5 - the Master's overriding authority and his express right to request the Company's assistance. Section 6 - effective communication and a working language understood by personnel. Sections 9 and 12 - non-conformity reporting and Company review.
retrieval_cards.why: Citing these is the difference between an answer about communication and an answer about the ISM Code.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What measures are required for contact between ship and office?
retrieval_cards.answer: A written procedure in the SMS held both ends; a 24-hour number answered by a person; a duty roster and call-out list with alternates; the Designated Person as primary route with authority to escalate; a standard initial report format; an agreed reporting interval thereafter; multiple independent means in a stated order; one point of contact each way; a timed log kept both ends; respect for the Master's overriding authority; and a maintained shore contact list.
retrieval_cards.why: The printed word is 'measures', so each item is a countable proposition.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What should the ship's initial report to the office contain?
retrieval_cards.answer: Ship's name, position, time, the nature of the incident, casualties, pollution, damage and stability condition, weather, immediate action taken, assistance required, and who is calling. An agreed interval for situation reports follows, so the office need not interrupt the Master and so silence is recognised as a signal.
retrieval_cards.why: A standard format is what stops essential information being forgotten under stress.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is most often forgotten under 'communication equipment'?
retrieval_cards.answer: Internal communications - the general alarm and public address, telephones between bridge, engine room and steering gear independent of main power, and portable intrinsically safe radios allocated to fire and enclosed-space teams. Most emergencies are lost internally rather than externally. Also emergency power and dispersed siting, so that one fire or flood does not remove every means at once.
retrieval_cards.why: Candidates reach for GMDSS and stop, when the question asks about measures rather than carriage requirements.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Name the GMDSS functions.
retrieval_cards.answer: Distress alerting; search and rescue coordinating communications; on-scene communications; locating signals; maritime safety information; and general communications.
retrieval_cards.why: Answering by function rather than by sea area is what the question asks for and avoids quoting a carriage table.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What measures are required for dealing with the media?
retrieval_cards.answer: A single named authorised spokesperson and an instruction that nobody else speaks; the Master and crew refer all enquiries to him; a prepared holding statement issued quickly, saying only that an incident has occurred and the company is responding; facts only, with no speculation as to cause and no admission of liability, on legal and P&I advice; no names released before the next of kin are informed; a single channel of release; monitoring of coverage including social media; and coordination with flag State, salvors, class and P&I.
retrieval_cards.why: It is a company function, not a shipboard one, and saying so is the first mark.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What measures are required for dealing with the next of kin?
retrieval_cards.answer: Accurate current records retrievable out of hours; named trained personnel to make contact, in the family's language where possible; contact as soon as facts are verified and before names reach the press; say only what is known and call back when promised; a single named point of contact per family; practical support - travel, accommodation, documents, repatriation, interpreters, counselling; clear information on entitlements handled with the P&I club without pressing anyone to sign; protection from the press; continued contact through the investigation; and no admissions of liability.
retrieval_cards.why: The governing principle is that the family hears it from the company, from a person, first, and accurately.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Does the ISM Code require a media plan or a next-of-kin procedure?
retrieval_cards.answer: Not expressly. Section 8 requires the Company to identify potential emergency situations, establish procedures to respond to them, run drills and exercises, and ensure the organisation can respond at any time. It says nothing about media handling, next-of-kin contact or equipment specification. Those are good management practice consistent with the Code, and what a competent procedure contains.
retrieval_cards.why: Stating the boundary between Code and practice shows judgement and avoids asserting as regulation something that is not in the Code.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How do the four printed items divide, and what tests them?
retrieval_cards.answer: Into two pairs. Ship-to-office contact and communication equipment are inward-facing - how the response is delivered. Media and next of kin are outward-facing - how the company is judged. Only paragraph 8.2, the programme of drills and exercises, tests whether any of it works before the day it is needed, and a failure found in a drill is a non-conformity under section 9.
retrieval_cards.why: It gives the answer a closing argument instead of stopping after the fourth list.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The four measure sets for items (i) to (iv) are good management practice consistent with the ISM Code, NOT requirements of the Code
reverify_before_publication.why: The Code requires that the Company identify emergency situations and establish procedures; it does not prescribe their content and says nothing about media handling, next-of-kin contact or equipment specification. The answer states this distinction openly. A later editor must not promote these measures to Code requirements, and must not add a paragraph number to any of them.

reverify_before_publication.claim: No GMDSS carriage requirement, sea area, equipment specification or SOLAS chapter IV regulation number is asserted; the equipment limb is answered by function
reverify_before_publication.why: MIW holds no licensed SOLAS text. The question asks what measures are required, which is a management question, not a carriage question. If carriage detail is ever added it must come from a held SOLAS text and must be the position at or before June 2023.

reverify_before_publication.claim: No drill frequency, response-time target or call-out interval is asserted
reverify_before_publication.why: Drill frequencies come from SOLAS and from company policy, not from the ISM Code, and MIW holds no SOLAS text. The answer requires that drills be programmed and realistic without asserting an interval.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The operative ISM section 8 at this sitting is paragraph 8.1 as amended by MSC.273(85), with 8.2 and 8.3 as originally adopted
reverify_before_publication.why: Established by reading the amendment chain this session rather than assuming it. Recorded so that a later editor neither reverts 8.1 to the 1993 wording nor supposes that 8.2 or 8.3 were amended. The 33rd Assembly ISM-related resolution of 6 December 2023 is six months FUTURE at this sitting and must not be introduced.

decomposition_gate.question_intent: Sixteen marks printed on the question, with four numbered items carrying no split. The stem prints TWO demands - 'underline the Importance of communication in emergency preparedness' and 'what measures are required for the following' - and both must be answered. The opening sentence is a near-verbatim lift of ISM paragraph 8.3, which tells you the examiner expects an ISM-based answer and not a general management essay. The four items divide naturally into inward-facing response delivery, items (i) and (ii), and outward-facing reputation and welfare, items (iii) and (iv).
decomposition_gate.mark_allocation: 16 marks, undivided across the four items and no split invented. Roughly four to five marks on the importance argument together with the ISM framing, because the stem gives it its own command verb, and the remainder spread across the four measure sets. Within those, the media and next-of-kin limbs deserve equal weight to the technical two: they are the halves most candidates under-write, and they are the halves where the marks are easiest to earn because the content is concrete.
decomposition_gate.examiner_expectation: That the candidate recognises his own opening sentence as ISM 8.3, knows that section 8 has three paragraphs and can cite the supporting sections - the Designated Person's direct access to the highest level of management, and the Master's overriding authority. On the four items, that he produces MEASURES rather than sentiments: a 24-hour number answered by a person, a standard initial report format, a single authorised spokesperson, and no names released before the next of kin are informed. A candidate who also states that the Code requires procedures to exist but does not prescribe their content has shown judgement the examiner will notice.
primary_source_plan: READ ISM SECTION 8 AT SOURCE AND COMPARE IT WORD BY WORD WITH THE PRINTED STEM - the suspicion that the examiner has lifted a paragraph must be confirmed, not assumed
CHECK THE AMENDMENT CHAIN FOR SECTION 8 rather than assuming stability - read the amending resolutions and establish which paragraph moved and which did not
Read sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 12 for the supporting framework, taking the actual wording of the Designated Person's access and the Master's overriding authority
Establish that no 33rd Assembly ISM instrument is in scope, since the 33rd Assembly is six months future at this sitting
Establish what the corpus holds for SOLAS before writing the equipment limb, and decide on that basis whether carriage detail may be asserted at all
Search specifically for 'emergency preparedness', 'next of kin' and media crisis handling before treating the four measure sets as fresh - the searches returned nothing, which is the finding
Draw and state the boundary between what the Code requires and what good practice supplies, before drafting the measure sets
decomposition_gate.freshness_risk: LOW - the ISM Code is the most temporally stable instrument on this paper - adopted 1993, and the most recent amendment set relevant to any part of this answer entered force in January 2015, eight years before this sitting. Nothing here moved during 2023. The only currency discipline required is negative: the 33rd Assembly of 6 December 2023 is six months future and none of its instruments may appear.
decomposition_gate.jurisdiction_risk: LOW. The ISM Code applies internationally through SOLAS chapter IX and India is a Party. No Indian statute is load-bearing; the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 governs the paper generally but is not engaged. The media and next-of-kin measures deliberately avoid any jurisdiction-specific legal proposition.
technical_ambiguities: Whether the opening sentence is the examiner's own words or the Code's - it is ISM 8.3, confirmed word by word
Whether element 8 requires media and next-of-kin procedures - it does not; it requires that response procedures exist
Whether communication equipment means GMDSS only - it does not; internal communications are at least as important
Whether media handling is a shipboard function - it is not; it is a company function with a single spokesperson
Whether the office may direct the emergency response - not against the Master's overriding authority under section 5
Which wording of paragraph 8.1 is operative - the amended one, established by reading the amending resolution
decomposition_gate.target_answer_shape: Open by identifying the stem as ISM 8.3 and setting out all three paragraphs of section 8, which costs four lines and frames everything. Then the importance argument as a sequence of linked propositions rather than as praise of communication in general. Then a short table of the supporting ISM sections, because five sections in a table cost the space of two in prose. Then the four measure sets as substantial bulleted lists, each bullet a measure, with the media limb opening on the fact that it is a company function and the next-of-kin limb opening on its single governing principle. Close by pairing the items - two inward, two outward - and returning to drills as the only test.
decomposition_gate.note: Command verbs -> command_verbs. Required answer components -> decomposition. Internal reuse map -> reuse_evidence. Not duplicated here.

blocks.h: 1. Why there are alternatives at all

blocks.p: The stem asks about alternatives to tin-based paints, so the ban is framing and not the answer. Keep it to four lines and move on.

ul: Tributyl tin (TBT) self-polishing copolymers were the most effective anti-foulings ever produced. They were also persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic at vanishingly low concentration - causing imposex in marine gastropods and shell deformation in oysters at levels far below those affecting the organisms they were meant to control.

The AFS Convention 2001, in force 17 September 2008, prohibits the application or re-application of organotin compounds acting as biocides in anti-fouling systems, and requires that a ship either does not bear such a system or carries a coating forming a barrier to its leaching.

The commercial problem the industry then had to solve is worth one sentence, because it explains all four alternatives: replace a biocide that worked extremely well, without losing the controlled, predictable release that made it work.

blocks.h: 2. The second ban, and why it bites on this question now

blocks.p: This is what makes the question current rather than historical, and it is the fact most candidates will not have. Resolution MEPC.331(76), adopted 17 June 2021, entered into force on 1 January 2023 and added cybutryne to the controlled list. From that date:

ul: anti-fouling systems containing cybutryne may not be applied or re-applied; and

a ship already bearing such a system must have it removed, or overcoated with a sealer coat that prevents leaching, at the next scheduled renewal of the anti-fouling system and in any event within 60 months of the last application.

blocks.p: The controls have been in force for about five months at this examination. Why it matters here: cybutryne was used as a booster biocide in some tin-free products, including self-polishing copolymer and hybrid formulations - two of the four types the examiner has named. The regulatory pressure on this question is on the biocidal alternatives, not on the tin they replaced.
It also sets up the comparison at the end: every biocidal system carries the risk that its biocide is next, and that risk is the strongest argument for the non-biocidal option.

blocks.h: 3. (i) Controlled Depletion Polymer (CDP)

rows: A soluble-matrix coating. The binder is a rosin-based or rosin-modified system which dissolves slowly in seawater, progressively exposing and releasing the biocide dispersed in it. The modern descendant of the traditional soluble-matrix paint, with the depletion rate controlled by the polymer chemistry rather than left to the rosin alone

The dissolved layer leaves a leached, porous skeleton at the surface. Release rate is not linear - highest when fresh, falling away as the leached layer thickens and diffusion through it becomes the limiting step

Cheapest of the four. Tolerant of poor surface preparation and of over-application. Easy to apply and to overcoat, and compatible with most existing schemes, which matters at a repair dock. Low capital cost suits short docking intervals and older or lower-value tonnage

Shortest effective life of the four, so it is not suited to long docking intervals. Performance degrades progressively rather than holding. The leached layer increases hull roughness, so the fuel penalty grows through the cycle. Poor at rest - it depends on water movement to erode and does not defend a ship lying idle. Rosin is somewhat brittle and water-sensitive
Coastal and short-sea trades, short docking cycles, vessels where first cost dominates

blocks.h: 4. (ii) Self-Polishing Copolymer (SPC)

rows: Chemical, not physical. The biocide - or a pendant group - is chemically bonded into an acrylate copolymer backbone. In slightly alkaline seawater the side group hydrolyses, making the surface layer soluble so it is washed away by the passing water, exposing fresh binder and fresh biocide beneath. This is the tin-free descendant of the TBT-SPC principle, using silyl, copper or zinc acrylate chemistry instead of tributyl tin

The defining feature is a controlled, near-linear polishing rate. The surface is continuously renewed, so release stays steady and no thick leached layer builds up - and the hull actually gets smoother in service rather than rougher

Long, predictable service life - the type that supports the longest docking intervals of the biocidal three. Consistent antifouling performance to the end of the cycle. Smoothing effect gives a real fuel benefit over the cycle. Predictable enough that the coating life can be matched to the docking plan

Dearer than CDP and demanding of surface preparation and application control. Polishing depends on water flow, so like CDP it performs poorly on a ship lying idle, and the rate varies with speed, temperature and salinity. It is still a biocidal system, so it carries regulatory exposure - which is exactly what the cybutryne control has just demonstrated
The workhorse of deep-sea trading - long voyages, steady speeds, long docking intervals

blocks.p: If one distinction is to be made clearly in this answer, make this one. CDP dissolves; SPC hydrolyses and is polished away by the water. That is why CDP roughens and SPC smooths, and it is the single sentence the examiner is looking for.

blocks.h: 5. (Ill) Hybrid TBT free paint

blocks.p: Note first what this category is not. It is not a paint containing some tin. It is a commercial blend of the two chemistries above - a binder combining rosin or rosin-derivative with a self-polishing copolymer component, in varying proportions.

ul: Principle. Both mechanisms operate together: some dissolution of the rosin fraction, some hydrolysis and polishing of the copolymer fraction. Adjusting the ratio moves the product along a continuous scale between CDP and full SPC.

Merits. Intermediate cost and intermediate life, which is exactly the point - it lets an owner buy a docking interval he actually needs instead of the one the product offers. More tolerant of application conditions than a full SPC, and generally easier to overcoat and more compatible with existing schemes at a repair yard. Commercially it lets a manufacturer offer a graded range on one platform.

Limits. It is a compromise and behaves like one: it neither polishes as cleanly as a true SPC nor costs as little as a CDP, and performance is less predictable because it depends on the blend. It still leaches to some extent and can still build a partial leached layer. And it remains biocidal, with the same regulatory exposure - hybrids were among the products that used cybutryne as a booster, so this category was directly affected by the control that came into force at the start of this year.
Where it fits. Mixed trading patterns, moderate docking intervals, and vessels where the full SPC premium is not justified by the operating profile.

blocks.h: 6. (iv) Fouling Release paint

blocks.p: This is the one genuine departure in the list. It is not a better biocide - it contains no biocide at all. It does not kill or poison fouling; it makes the surface one that fouling cannot adhere strongly to.

ul: Principle. A silicone elastomer - or a fluoropolymer - giving a very low surface energy, very smooth, slightly flexible, non-stick surface. Organisms that do settle attach weakly and are sheared off by the water flow once the ship is up to speed, or removed by gentle cleaning.

Merits. No biocide, so it sits outside the biocidal regulatory pressure entirely - the strongest single argument in its favour in a year in which a second biocide has just been banned. The smoothest surface of the four, giving the lowest frictional resistance, which is a direct fuel and carbon-intensity benefit. Long life - it is not consumed, so it does not deplete, and it can last several docking cycles. Cleaning is easier and less damaging.

Limits. Highest first cost, often by a wide margin. It requires a full multi-coat scheme - tie coat over the anticorrosive, then the topcoat - and exacting surface preparation and application; it is essentially a newbuilding or major-refit decision rather than something applied at any dock. It is mechanically soft and easily damaged by ice, contact and careless brush cleaning, and local repair is difficult because nothing adheres well to it, including new paint. Above all, it depends on speed: below a threshold service speed there is insufficient shear to release the fouling, so it is poor for slow ships and for ships that lie idle for long periods.

Where it fits. Fast, high-utilisation, deep-sea ships with long docking intervals - container ships, car carriers, LNG carriers - and increasingly any owner for whom hull smoothness is now a carbon-intensity question.

blocks.h: 7. Choosing between them

blocks.p: The four are not four grades of the same product. They are two biocidal families, one commercial blend of them, and one non-biocidal principle - and once that grouping is stated the comparison writes itself.

The selection factors that actually decide it in practice are the trading pattern and the docking interval: service speed and how much of the time the ship is actually making it; the proportion of idle and port time, since three of the four need water flow and the fourth needs speed; water temperature and fouling severity on the route; the interval to the next docking, because there is no merit in buying coating life you will not use; whether this is a newbuilding or an in-service repaint, since the compatibility of an overcoat with the existing scheme may exclude an option outright; and the surface preparation the yard can actually deliver.

blocks.h: 8. What else is in the field, and why this is now a fuel question

ul: Copper-based and copper-free biocidal systems using organic booster biocides, and increasingly zinc chemistry - the mainstream tin-free biocidal market from which the four named types are drawn.
Hydrogel and hydrophilic-modified coatings, which combine a fouling-release surface with an enhanced water layer.

Hard, inert, non-toxic coatings used with planned in-water cleaning - a different trade: no biocide and no depletion, but a scheduled cleaning regime instead, and a growing regulatory issue in its own right because cleaning releases what was on the hull.
Non-coating approaches - ultrasonic and UV systems, and hull-form or niche-area design to reduce sheltered fouling sites.

blocks.p: Close on the point that gives the question its present importance. Fouling is now a fuel and emissions question as much as an environmental one. Fouling and roughness increase frictional resistance and therefore consumption and carbon intensity, and the operational carbon-intensity regime entered into force at the beginning of this year. So the coating decision is no longer only about protecting the sea from the paint - it is about the ship's measured operating efficiency across the whole docking cycle. That is why the smoothing behaviour of a self-polishing copolymer, and the low friction of a fouling release surface, are now selection criteria and not merely technical curiosities.

blocks.h: Why this structure scores

blocks.p: This question prints no marks, four named types and a single command verb, "discuss". That looks generous and is actually a trap: with sixteen marks and four named limbs there is room for real depth on each, and a candidate who writes four short paragraphs of general description will use half the available marks. The route therefore gives each type its own step with a consistent four-heading treatment - principle, behaviour, merits, limits - and then adds a comparison step and a wider-field step, which are where the discriminating marks are.

Note what the stem does not ask. It does not ask about the Anti-Fouling Convention, the certificate, the declaration or the records. Those belong to a different printing of this material. Here the Convention is framing only, worth four lines, because the words "alternatives to tin-based" require you to say what was banned and why - and nothing more.

blocks.h: The one sentence that separates the top answers

blocks.p: CDP dissolves; SPC hydrolyses and is polished away by the moving water. Everything else about the two follows from it - why CDP roughens as its leached layer builds and SPC smooths, why CDP's release rate falls away and SPC's stays steady, why CDP is cheap and short-lived and SPC is dear and long-lived. If you can write that one line and then derive the consequences, you have shown mechanism rather than memory.

blocks.h: What 'hybrid TBT free' actually means

blocks.p: Almost every weak answer to this question gets the third type wrong, usually by implying it contains some reduced amount of tin. It does not. A hybrid is a blend of the CDP and SPC binder chemistries - rosin or rosin derivative plus a self-polishing copolymer component - in a chosen ratio, so the product sits at a chosen point on the scale between them. "TBT free" is in the name for historical and marketing reasons, distinguishing it from the tin-based hybrids of the past.
Say that explicitly, and add the commercial reason the category exists: it lets an owner buy the docking interval he needs rather than the one the product offers.

blocks.h: Fouling release is a different principle, not a better paint

blocks.p: The fourth type is the only one that is not a biocidal system at all, and treating it as "the expensive one" misses the point. It kills nothing. It presents a low-surface-energy, non-stick, elastomeric surface to which fouling adheres so weakly that water flow shears it off.

That single fact generates all its merits and all its limits at once: no biocide means no regulatory exposure and no depletion, hence long life and the smoothest hull; but non-stick also means nothing else sticks to it either, hence difficult repair and demanding application, and shear-dependence means it is poor for slow ships and ships that lie idle. Deriving both halves from one property is what a "discuss" answer is for.

blocks.h: The current fact almost nobody will have

blocks.p: Cybutryne was added to the controlled list by MEPC.331(76) and the control entered into force on 1 January 2023 - about five months before this examination. From that date it may not be applied or re-applied, and an existing system containing it must be removed or sealed over at the next scheduled renewal of the anti-fouling system and in any event within 60 months of the last application.

It is worth a mark twice over. First, because it is genuinely current at this sitting. Second, because it lands on the biocidal types - cybutryne was used as a booster biocide in some SPC and hybrid products - which means the regulatory pressure in this question is now on the alternatives, not on the tin they replaced. That is the observation that makes the whole answer feel contemporary, and it is what justifies the closing argument for the non-biocidal option.

blocks.h: Why this is also a fuel question

blocks.p: Fouling and roughness raise frictional resistance, which raises consumption, which raises carbon intensity - and the operational carbon-intensity requirements came into force at the beginning of this same year. So coating selection is now an energy-efficiency decision measured across the docking cycle, which is why the smoothing behaviour of an SPC and the low friction of a fouling release surface have become selection criteria rather than technical footnotes. One paragraph on this at the end lifts the answer out of the paint shop.

blocks.h: Common mistakes

ul: Writing a long answer on the Anti-Fouling Convention, the certificate and the records. Not asked here.
Describing CDP and SPC as the same mechanism at different speeds. One dissolves, the other hydrolyses and polishes.
Saying CDP gets smoother with age. It roughens - the leached layer is the reason.
Implying a hybrid contains some tin. It is a blend of the two tin-free binder chemistries.
Calling fouling release a biocidal paint, or a "very good antifouling". It contains no biocide and kills nothing.
Omitting that fouling release is speed-dependent and therefore poor for slow or idle ships - the limitation examiners ask about most.
Not knowing about cybutryne, which is the one genuinely current regulatory fact available here.
Quoting service lives in months or fuel savings as percentages. These are product-specific, commercial and easy to get wrong.
Naming manufacturers or products.
Giving four descriptions and no comparison. With sixteen marks and no printed split, the comparison is where the top band is.

blocks.h: Examiner traps

ul: "Does a hybrid contain tin?" No. It is a blend of rosin-based and self-polishing copolymer chemistries.
"Which coating gets smoother in service, and why?" SPC - the surface is continuously renewed by hydrolysis and shear, so no leached layer accumulates.
"Your ship lies at anchor for two months. Which coating suffers most?" All the flow-dependent ones suffer, but fouling release suffers most - it needs speed to shear the fouling off.
"How does fouling release work?" Low surface energy and elasticity; weak adhesion; fouling is sheared off by flow. No biocide.
"Why is fouling release hard to repair?" Because nothing adheres well to it - including new paint.
"What changed in anti-fouling regulation this year?" Cybutryne controls entered into force on 1 January 2023.

"What must a ship do if her existing system contains cybutryne?" Remove it or apply a sealer coat at the next scheduled renewal of the anti-fouling system, and within 60 months of the last application.
"Which of the four is outside biocidal regulation?" Fouling release - and that is now a commercial argument, not just an environmental one.
"Which would you choose for a short-sea vessel with a two-year docking cycle?" CDP or a rosin-rich hybrid - there is no merit in buying coating life you will not use.

blocks.h: Likely oral follow-up

ul: Why were tin-based antifoulings banned? Persistence, bioaccumulation, imposex in gastropods and shell deformation in oysters at very low concentrations.
When did the AFS Convention enter into force? 17 September 2008.
How does a CDP work? A rosin-based soluble matrix dissolves in seawater, exposing and releasing the biocide dispersed in it.
How does an SPC work? The biocide or a pendant group is chemically bonded into an acrylate copolymer; hydrolysis in seawater makes the surface layer soluble and it is polished away by the flow.
Which chemistries replaced tributyl tin in SPCs? Silyl, copper and zinc acrylates.
What is a hybrid? A blend of rosin and self-polishing copolymer binders, giving intermediate cost, life and predictability.
How does fouling release differ in principle? It contains no biocide; low surface energy and elasticity make adhesion weak so fouling is sheared off by flow.
What are its two main practical drawbacks? Speed dependence, and mechanical vulnerability with difficult local repair.
What is cybutryne and what happened to it? A booster biocide, added to the controlled list by MEPC.331(76), controls in force 1 January 2023.
How does coating choice affect the ship's carbon intensity? Through hull roughness and fouling, which raise frictional resistance and consumption across the docking cycle.

blocks.h: Memory framework

blocks.p: Group them before you describe them: TWO BIOCIDAL FAMILIES, ONE BLEND, ONE NON-STICK. That is the whole taxonomy and it stops the four blurring together.

For the mechanisms, four verbs: DISSOLVES · POLISHES · BOTH · RELEASES. For the surface with age, three words: ROUGHENS · SMOOTHS · SMOOTHEST. For cost and life, remember they run together: CHEAP AND SHORT · DEAR AND LONG · MIDDLE · DEAREST AND LONGEST.
Treat every type under the same four headings - PRINCIPLE, BEHAVIOUR, MERITS, LIMITS - so the answer is visibly systematic and nothing is forgotten under one type that was remembered under another.

blocks.h: Regulation and source map

ul: AFS Convention 2001 - adopted October 2001, in force 17 September 2008
AFS Annex 1 - organotin compounds acting as biocides: not applied or re-applied; otherwise a barrier coating

AFS Annex 4 - survey and certification; International Anti-Fouling System Certificate for 400 GT and above on international voyages; Declaration for 24 m and above but under 400 GT. Framing only - not asked on this paper

Resolution MEPC.358(78) - 2022 Guidelines for survey and certification of anti-fouling systems; the operative guidance at this sitting
Coating chemistry and behaviour - industry guidance, stated qualitatively; no service life, polishing rate, saving percentage or price asserted

blocks.h: Uncertainty and the boundary between regulation and industry practice

blocks.p: The regulatory half of this answer is verified. The AFS Convention position and the cybutryne chain come from MIW's own verification record for a sitting at which the Convention itself was read, and the elapsed interval was recalculated for this examination rather than carried across - about five months, not the days that were correct for a January 2023 sitting and not the fifteen months that will be correct for an April 2024 one. The boundary is day-independent here: the controls took effect on the first day of January and this sitting is in June, so no reasoning about the examination day is needed.

The coating technology itself is industry guidance and the answer says so. Release mechanisms, polishing behaviour, relative service life and surface-energy behaviour are drawn from coating-manufacturer technical literature and are stated qualitatively. Accordingly no service life in months, no polishing or leaching rate, no dry-film thickness, no fuel-saving percentage and no price comparison is asserted anywhere, and no product or manufacturer is named. Relative behaviour - which type holds performance longer, which roughens, which is dearest - is what the question asks for, and it is what is given.

One instruction for a later editor: the Convention-and-documents material must not be added back into this answer. It belongs to a different printing of the same limb, which prints a second limb this paper does not. Adding it would spend half a sixteen-mark question on something the examiner did not ask.

notes: THE RISK ON THIS QUESTION RUNS BACKWARDS, AS IT DOES ON EVERY PRINTING OF THIS LIMB. The danger is OMITTING something already in force, not importing something later. The cybutryne controls under MEPC.331(76) entered into force on 1 JANUARY 2023 and are therefore FIVE MONTHS OLD at this examination. An answer written from pre-2023 material would miss them entirely, and they are the single most current fact available on this question.

THE ELAPSED INTERVAL WAS RECALCULATED FOR THIS SITTING AND NOT INHERITED FROM EITHER NEIGHBOUR. The January 2023 donor correctly records the controls as DAYS old; the April 2024 printing correctly records them as FIFTEEN MONTHS old. Neither figure is true here. At June 2023 the correct statement is about FIVE MONTHS, and the answer states the maturity accordingly - the first removal and sealer-coat decisions have been taken in practice, which was not true in January.

THE BOUNDARY IS DAY-INDEPENDENT AND THAT WAS CHECKED DELIBERATELY. The paper prints JUNE 2023 with no day. Because the controls entered into force on 1 JANUARY 2023, every possible sitting day in June falls well after that date, so no reasoning about the examination day is required and none is used. This is the easy case; the January 2023 printing had to reason about it explicitly because the entry into force fell in its own sitting month.

THE GUIDELINES EDITION WAS CHECKED. MEPC.358(78), the 2022 Guidelines for survey and certification of anti-fouling systems, was adopted in June 2022 and is the operative guidance at this sitting. No later edition is referenced.

DELIBERATELY ABSENT, ALL FUTURE. Nothing from MEPC 80 of 3 to 7 JULY 2023 or later is used - MEPC 80 is ONE MONTH after this sitting. No 33rd Assembly resolution is cited; the 33rd Assembly did not adopt until 6 December 2023. The Hong Kong Convention is not mentioned in connection with coating removal, because it is not in force at this sitting.

THE DONOR RUNS THE RIGHT WAY AND THE TWO LATER PRINTINGS WERE REJECTED FOR THAT REASON. QP2301-Q2 is JANUARY 2023 - five months EARLIER, same year, same regime. QP2404-Q5 (April 2024) and QP2409-Q8 (September 2024) print the identical limb but are LATER, and QP2404-Q5's own record describes a market maturity that did not exist in June 2023. Neither was used as the donor.

THE ENERGY-EFFICIENCY LINK AT STEP 8 WAS RE-ANCHORED. The operational carbon-intensity regime entered into force on 1 JANUARY 2023, so at this sitting it is in its FIRST data year and NO SHIP HAS YET BEEN RATED. The answer says that coating choice bears on measured operating efficiency; it does NOT refer to rating experience, to any rating distribution, or to the 2023 IMO GHG Strategy, which was adopted on 7 July 2023 and is ONE MONTH FUTURE at this sitting.
MERCHANT SHIPPING ACT, 1958 governs at this sitting; the 2025 Act is thirty-three months future. Neither is load-bearing on this question.

That is recorded here because it is the kind of error an exact-recurrence relation invites.

AT THIS SITTING THE CONTROLS ARE ABOUT FIVE MONTHS OLD
cybutryne was a BOOSTER BIOCIDE in some SPC and HYBRID products - two of the four types named
THE REGULATORY PRESSURE IS NOW ON THE BIOCIDAL ALTERNATIVES, NOT ON THE TIN THEY REPLACED
sets up the closing argument - every biocidal system carries the risk that its biocide is next

steps.title: (i) Controlled Depletion Polymer (CDP)
points: PRINCIPLE - a SOLUBLE MATRIX. A rosin-based binder DISSOLVES in seawater, exposing and releasing the biocide dispersed in it
the modern descendant of the traditional soluble-matrix paint, with depletion controlled by the polymer chemistry
BEHAVIOUR - leaves a LEACHED POROUS SKELETON; release is NOT LINEAR, highest when fresh and falling as the leached layer thickens
MERITS - CHEAPEST; tolerant of poor surface preparation; easy to apply and overcoat; COMPATIBLE WITH MOST EXISTING SCHEMES
LIMITS - SHORTEST LIFE; performance DEGRADES progressively; the leached layer INCREASES HULL ROUGHNESS so the fuel penalty grows
LIMITS - POOR AT REST; depends on water movement; rosin is brittle and water-sensitive
WHERE IT FITS - coastal and short-sea trades, short docking cycles, first cost dominant

steps.title: (ii) Self-Polishing Copolymer (SPC)
points: PRINCIPLE - CHEMICAL, NOT PHYSICAL. The biocide or pendant group is CHEMICALLY BONDED into an acrylate copolymer backbone
in slightly alkaline seawater the side group HYDROLYSES, the surface layer becomes soluble and is WASHED AWAY BY THE PASSING WATER, exposing fresh binder and biocide
the tin-free descendant of TBT-SPC using SILYL, COPPER OR ZINC ACRYLATE chemistry
BEHAVIOUR - a CONTROLLED, NEAR-LINEAR POLISHING RATE; steady release; NO THICK LEACHED LAYER; THE HULL GETS SMOOTHER IN SERVICE
MERITS - LONG PREDICTABLE LIFE, supports the longest docking intervals of the biocidal three; consistent performance to the end of the cycle; smoothing gives a real fuel benefit
LIMITS - DEARER and demanding of surface preparation and application control
LIMITS - polishing depends on WATER FLOW, so poor when idle; rate varies with SPEED, TEMPERATURE AND SALINITY; STILL BIOCIDAL, with the regulatory exposure cybutryne has just demonstrated
THE KEY SENTENCE: CDP DISSOLVES; SPC HYDROLYSES AND IS POLISHED AWAY BY THE WATER

steps.title: (Ill) Hybrid TBT free paint
points: IT IS NOT A PAINT CONTAINING SOME TIN - it is a COMMERCIAL BLEND of the two chemistries above
binder combines ROSIN OR ROSIN DERIVATIVE with a SELF-POLISHING COPOLYMER component, in varying proportions
PRINCIPLE - both mechanisms operate together; adjusting the ratio moves the product along a scale between CDP and full SPC
MERITS - INTERMEDIATE COST AND LIFE, which is the point: buy the docking interval you actually need
MERITS - more tolerant of application conditions than a full SPC; easier to overcoat and more compatible at a repair yard; lets a manufacturer offer a graded range on one platform
LIMITS - a COMPROMISE THAT BEHAVES LIKE ONE; neither polishes as cleanly nor costs as little; LESS PREDICTABLE because it depends on the blend
LIMITS - still leaches and can build a partial leached layer; STILL BIOCIDAL - hybrids were among the products using CYBUTRYNE as a booster
WHERE IT FITS - mixed trading, moderate docking intervals, where the full SPC premium is not justified

steps.title: (iv) Fouling Release paint
points: THE ONE GENUINE DEPARTURE - IT IS NOT A BETTER BIOCIDE, IT CONTAINS NO BIOCIDE AT ALL
PRINCIPLE - a SILICONE ELASTOMER or fluoropolymer giving VERY LOW SURFACE ENERGY, very smooth, slightly flexible, non-stick
organisms that settle attach WEAKLY and are SHEARED OFF BY THE WATER FLOW once the ship is up to speed
MERITS - NO BIOCIDE, so outside biocidal regulatory pressure entirely - the strongest argument in a year when a second biocide has just been banned
MERITS - SMOOTHEST SURFACE OF THE FOUR, lowest frictional resistance, a direct fuel and carbon-intensity benefit
MERITS - LONG LIFE; it is not consumed and does not deplete; can last several docking cycles; easier, less damaging cleaning
LIMITS - HIGHEST FIRST COST; requires a FULL MULTI-COAT SCHEME with a tie coat and exacting preparation; essentially a newbuilding or major-refit decision
LIMITS - MECHANICALLY SOFT and easily damaged; LOCAL REPAIR IS DIFFICULT because nothing adheres well to it, including new paint
LIMITS - IT DEPENDS ON SPEED. Below a threshold service speed there is insufficient shear, so POOR FOR SLOW SHIPS AND SHIPS THAT LIE IDLE
WHERE IT FITS - fast, high-utilisation, deep-sea ships with long docking intervals

steps.title: Choosing between them
points: THE FOUR ARE NOT FOUR GRADES OF THE SAME PRODUCT - they are TWO BIOCIDAL FAMILIES, ONE BLEND OF THEM, AND ONE NON-BIOCIDAL PRINCIPLE
MECHANISM - dissolves / hydrolyses and polishes / both / non-stick and sheared off
SURFACE WITH AGE - roughens / smooths / intermediate / smoothest throughout
LIFE AND COST run together - shortest and cheapest / long and dear / intermediate / longest and dearest
ALL FOUR ARE FLOW-DEPENDENT AND ALL PERFORM POORLY AT REST; fouling release is the worst of them for a slow or idle ship
REGULATORY EXPOSURE - biocidal, biocidal, biocidal, effectively none

SELECTION FACTORS - trading pattern and service speed; proportion of idle and port time; water temperature and fouling severity; INTERVAL TO NEXT DOCKING; newbuilding versus in-service repaint and overcoat compatibility; the surface preparation the yard can deliver
there is no merit in buying coating life you will not use

steps.title: What else is in the field, and why this is now a fuel question
points: COPPER-BASED AND COPPER-FREE biocidal systems with organic booster biocides, and increasingly ZINC chemistry
HYDROGEL AND HYDROPHILIC-MODIFIED coatings combining fouling release with an enhanced water layer
HARD, INERT, NON-TOXIC coatings used with PLANNED IN-WATER CLEANING - no biocide and no depletion, but a scheduled cleaning regime, and a growing regulatory issue in itself
NON-COATING approaches - ultrasonic and UV systems; hull-form and niche-area design to reduce sheltered fouling sites
FOULING IS NOW A FUEL AND EMISSIONS QUESTION AS MUCH AS AN ENVIRONMENTAL ONE
fouling and roughness raise frictional resistance, consumption and carbon intensity; the operational carbon-intensity regime came into force at the start of this year
so coating choice is now about MEASURED OPERATING EFFICIENCY ACROSS THE DOCKING CYCLE - which is why SPC smoothing and fouling-release friction are selection criteria and not curiosities

questions.understand_first: The whole subject exists because the best antifouling ever invented turned out to be poisoning everything around the ship at concentrations so small that nobody had thought to look. Once it was outlawed, the industry had to reproduce what made it so good - not the poison itself, but the trick of releasing a poison at a steady, controlled rate for years - and the four things this question names are four answers to that problem, of which only three are really the same kind of answer. Two of them work by wearing away. In the cheaper one the paint film simply dissolves in seawater, uncovering more of the poison mixed into it as it goes; because it leaves behind a spongy skeleton of what would not dissolve, the hull grows rougher as the years pass and the release tails off. In the better one the poison is chemically built into the binder itself, and a chemical reaction with seawater loosens the outermost skin so that the passing water carries it away, exposing a fresh face beneath; the release stays even and the hull actually gets smoother. The third is simply a mixture of the two recipes in whatever proportion suits the price and the docking interval an owner wants. The fourth is a complete change of thinking: instead of poisoning what lands on the hull, make the hull so slippery that nothing can hold on, and let the ship's own speed wash it off. That last idea escapes the regulatory problem entirely, which matters more each time another biocide is outlawed - but it only works if the ship actually goes fast, and it is expensive and fragile. Underneath all of it is a newer commercial fact: a rough or fouled hull now costs measurable fuel and shows up in the ship's efficiency figures, so choosing a coating is no longer just about protecting the sea from the paint.
questions.memory_cue: Group first: TWO BIOCIDAL FAMILIES, ONE BLEND, ONE NON-STICK (7). Four verbs for the mechanisms - DISSOLVES (3), POLISHES (4), BOTH (5), RELEASES (6). Treat every type under the same four headings, PRINCIPLE, BEHAVIOUR, MERITS, LIMITS. And carry the current fact: CYBUTRYNE, IN FORCE THIS JANUARY (2).

quick_revision.critical_regulation: The AFS Convention 2001, in force 17 September 2008, prohibits the application or re-application of organotin compounds acting as biocides in anti-fouling systems, requiring instead that a ship either bears no such system or carries a coating forming a barrier to leaching. Resolution MEPC.331(76), adopted 17 June 2021 and in force 1 January 2023, extends the controlled list to cybutryne: it may not be applied or re-applied, and an existing system containing it must be removed or overcoated with a sealer coat at the next scheduled renewal of the anti-fouling system and in any event within 60 months of the last application.
quick_revision.major_trap: Two traps, and the first is about marks rather than knowledge. This stem asks only about the four coating types - it does not ask about the Anti-Fouling Convention, the certificate or the records - so a candidate who has revised the two-limb version of this question will spend half a sixteen-mark answer on material nobody asked for. The technical traps are: describing CDP and SPC as the same mechanism at different speeds, when one dissolves and the other hydrolyses and is polished away - which is why CDP roughens and SPC smooths; implying a hybrid contains some tin when it is a blend of the two tin-free binder chemistries; treating fouling release as a very good antifouling paint when it contains no biocide and kills nothing; and omitting that fouling release is speed-dependent and therefore poor for slow or idle ships. Finally, not knowing about cybutryne - in force since 1 January 2023 - forfeits the one genuinely current fact on the question.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give the route for the alternatives-to-tin antifouling question.
retrieval_cards.answer: 1 Why alternatives exist - the tin ban, briefly. 2 The cybutryne control, in force this January. 3 CDP. 4 SPC. 5 Hybrid. 6 Fouling release. 7 Comparison and selection. 8 The wider field and the fuel link. Each type gets the same four headings - principle, behaviour, merits, limits.
retrieval_cards.why: Sixteen marks with no printed split; the comparison at step 7 is where the top band is, and step 1 must stay short.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Distinguish the mechanism of a controlled depletion polymer from a self-polishing copolymer.
retrieval_cards.answer: A CDP is a soluble matrix: a rosin-based binder dissolves in seawater, progressively exposing and releasing the biocide dispersed in it, leaving a leached porous layer behind. An SPC is chemical: the biocide or a pendant group is chemically bonded into an acrylate copolymer, and hydrolysis in seawater makes the surface layer soluble so it is polished away by the passing water, exposing fresh binder beneath.
retrieval_cards.why: This one distinction generates every difference between the two, including roughness and service life.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which of the four gets rougher in service and which gets smoother, and why?
retrieval_cards.answer: CDP roughens, because the undissolved fraction remains as a leached porous skeleton that accumulates. SPC smooths, because the surface is continuously renewed by hydrolysis and shear so no leached layer builds up. Fouling release is the smoothest of all throughout, being neither consumed nor depleted.
retrieval_cards.why: It converts a chemistry point into a fuel-consumption consequence, which is where the marks now are.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Does a hybrid TBT-free paint contain tin?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. It is a blend of the two tin-free binder chemistries - rosin or a rosin derivative together with a self-polishing copolymer component - in a chosen ratio, so the product sits at a chosen point on the scale between CDP and full SPC. 'TBT free' is in the name to distinguish it from the tin-based hybrids of the past.
retrieval_cards.why: Almost every weak answer implies the hybrid retains some tin.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How does a fouling release coating work, and what is it made of?
retrieval_cards.answer: It contains no biocide. A silicone elastomer or fluoropolymer presents a very low surface energy, very smooth, slightly flexible non-stick surface, so organisms that settle adhere weakly and are sheared off by the water flow once the ship is up to speed, or removed by gentle cleaning.
retrieval_cards.why: It is the only one of the four that is a different principle rather than a different chemistry.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Give the three practical limitations of a fouling release coating and derive them from one property.
retrieval_cards.answer: All three follow from its non-stick, soft, low-energy surface. It is speed-dependent - below a threshold service speed there is insufficient shear, so it is poor for slow ships and ships lying idle. It is mechanically soft and easily damaged. And local repair is difficult because nothing adheres well to it, including new paint. Add the high first cost and the need for a full multi-coat scheme with exacting preparation.
retrieval_cards.why: Deriving merits and limits from one property is what the command verb 'discuss' is asking for.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is cybutryne and what happened to it?
retrieval_cards.answer: A booster biocide used in some tin-free anti-fouling products. Resolution MEPC.331(76), adopted 17 June 2021, added it to the AFS Convention controlled list with effect from 1 January 2023. From that date it may not be applied or re-applied, and an existing system containing it must be removed or overcoated with a sealer coat at the next scheduled renewal of the anti-fouling system and within 60 months of the last application.
retrieval_cards.why: It is the one genuinely current regulatory fact available on this question at this sitting.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Why does the cybutryne control matter specifically to this question?
retrieval_cards.answer: Because it falls on the biocidal alternatives, not on the tin they replaced. Cybutryne was used as a booster biocide in some self-polishing copolymer and hybrid products - two of the four types the examiner names - so the regulatory pressure has moved onto the substitutes. It is also the strongest argument for the non-biocidal option: every biocidal system carries the risk that its biocide is next.
retrieval_cards.why: It turns a list of paints into an argument about where the technology is heading.

retrieval_cards.prompt: State the AFS Convention position on organotins and its entry into force.
retrieval_cards.answer: The Convention was adopted in October 2001 and entered into force on 17 September 2008. Organotin compounds acting as biocides in anti-fouling systems shall not be applied or re-applied, and a ship shall either not bear such a system or shall carry a coating forming a barrier to its leaching.
retrieval_cards.why: Framing only on this paper - the certificate and records limb is not printed here.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How do the four types group, and what decides the choice in practice?
retrieval_cards.answer: Two biocidal families - CDP and SPC - one commercial blend of them, and one non-biocidal principle. The choice is decided by trading pattern and service speed, the proportion of idle and port time, water temperature and fouling severity on the route, the interval to the next docking, whether it is a newbuilding or an in-service repaint with overcoat compatibility to consider, and the surface preparation the yard can actually deliver.
retrieval_cards.why: Stating the grouping first is what makes the comparison answerable in the space available.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Your ship trades short-sea with a two-year docking cycle. Which coating and why?
retrieval_cards.answer: A CDP or a rosin-rich hybrid. There is no merit in buying coating life that will not be used, the first cost is lowest, application is tolerant, and overcoating at a repair yard is easy. A fouling release scheme would be the wrong choice on cost, on the difficulty of application in a repair dock, and above all on speed - short-sea trading with much manoeuvring and port time gives too little shear to release the fouling.
retrieval_cards.why: The examiner wants a selection judgement, not four descriptions.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Why is coating choice now an energy-efficiency question?
retrieval_cards.answer: Because fouling and hull roughness increase frictional resistance, and therefore fuel consumption and carbon intensity, across the whole docking cycle - and the operational carbon-intensity requirements entered into force at the beginning of this same year. So the smoothing behaviour of a self-polishing copolymer and the low friction of a fouling release surface have become selection criteria rather than technical footnotes.
retrieval_cards.why: It lifts the answer out of the paint shop and connects it to the rest of the paper.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The cybutryne controls under MEPC.331(76) entered into force on 1 January 2023 and are about FIVE MONTHS old at this sitting

reverify_before_publication.why: Only the AFS Convention limits and the cybutryne control are regulatory. MIW holds no coating standard, ISO reference or test method, so none is cited. The distinction is stated in the answer itself and must not be blurred by a later editor attaching a regulation to a coating property.

If a figure is ever added it must be sourced, dated and tied to a stated set of operating conditions.

The stem's opening words, 'alternatives to tin-based antifouling paints', require a short statement of what was banned and why, and nothing more: the Convention, the certificate and the records are NOT asked for on this paper, although they are printed as a separate limb in another printing of this same material.
